findings.title: OrderKey restored by the version-change branch is never bounds-checked against the archive's column count; PGresult.sort panics
findings.description:
The reset added at report/report.go:299-301 re-arms `orderConfigured` and restores `v.OrderKey = seedOrderKey`. That value flows into countDiff (report/report.go:342) -> stat.Compare -> calculateDelta -> (*PGresult).sort, which indexes `r.Values[i][key]` with no bounds check on `key`. `PGresult.validate()` (internal/stat/postgres.go:558-572) only checks that every row width equals len(Cols) and that Nrows equals len(Values) - it never checks that the sort key is inside the row, and OrderKey seeds come from view.New() (0 for activity, 2 for progress_index, 4 for the statements_* screens), not from the archive.

Assessment of the specific question asked in the task hints: the reset does NOT introduce a new class of unchecked index. The same seed is the OrderKey from process start (newApp -> app.view), and the -o path is safe because getColumnIndex resolves against the very sample being printed. What the reset does is re-enter an already-unguarded path mid-stream, so the pre-existing hazard is not closed by this task either.

Verified empirically against a throwaway copy of the worktree (repo untouched):
- a crafted archive whose activity.* entries carry `Cols: []` and one empty row passes NewPGresultFile/validate and panics end-to-end through report.processData -> countDiff -> stat.sort with `index out of range [0] with length 0` - no version change required at all;
- direct call: `stat.Compare` on a 2-column result with orderKey 4 (the statements_* seed) panics with `index out of range [4] with length 2`.
The missing check is present at HEAD (`sample := r.Values[0][key].String`), i.e. it is pre-existing and is not caused by the sibling Task 01/02 edits to internal/stat/postgres.go.

Same DoS family as resolved debt [009] and as the zero-width guard this task lands: a process abort while parsing an archive an operator received from a colleague.
findings.location: internal/stat/postgres.go:678-693 ((*PGresult).sort), reached from report/report.go:342; index restored at report/report.go:300
findings.impact: A crafted or corrupted recording aborts `pgcenter report` with an unrecoverable runtime panic instead of an error message. Availability only - no memory disclosure, no code execution, no privilege boundary crossed (the operator already chose to open the file). Reachable on any report type, with or without -o, and without any version change in the archive.

findings.title: The new guard's error return aborts processData and leaves readTar blocked - the report pipeline hangs instead of failing
findings.description:
The guard converts `slice bounds out of range [:-1]` into `return 0, fmt.Errorf("zero or negative width, skip")`, which processData propagates with a bare `return err` (report/report.go:357-360). processData never drains or closes dataCh on its error paths, so readTar stays blocked on the unbuffered `dataCh <- data{...}` (report/report.go:223) and doReport's `wg.Wait()` (report/report.go:135) never returns.

Verified: an archive whose column count grows between two samples of the SAME version (no version boundary, so the new resets do not apply, alignment stays latched and ColsWidth has no key for the extra indices) reaches the guard. Through processData directly the guard works as intended - an error, no panic. Through the real `doReport` pipeline the same archive produced no return within 5 seconds, i.e. the command hangs.

This is the pre-existing shape of every error path in processData (countDiff, printStatHeader, the procpidstat warning path), not something the guard invented - the new test helper `runProcessDataOnTar` documents the same behaviour and works around it with a drain goroutine. But the guard does add a new archive-triggerable entry into that shape, so the crash-DoS is mitigated into a hang-DoS rather than into a clean error for that particular archive. Note the twin in top/printDataCell returns the same error into an interactive refresh loop where a bad frame is skipped and the process survives; report/ has no such loop.
findings.impact: `pgcenter report` on a crafted archive hangs indefinitely (or, depending on goroutine state, aborts with a runtime deadlock error) instead of printing an error and exiting non-zero. Local availability only; the operator can Ctrl-C.

findings.title: PGresult.Ncols is decoded from the archive and never reconciled with len(Cols), so the diff loop indexes past the real row width
findings.description:
Context for the task's claim that debt [020] does not become reachable. That claim is correct with respect to version changes - the version-change branch still replaces prevStat with the new sample, so curr/prev are always the same version - and this diff does not change it. However [020] is reachable in two crafted-archive ways that have nothing to do with version changes, and the changed code does not address them:

1. `validate()` checks row width against len(Cols) but never against the separately-decoded `Ncols` field. `diff()` loops `for l := 0; l < curr.Ncols; l++` and reads `curr.Values[i][l]`. Verified: a result with `Ncols: 999`, two real columns and a matching unique key panics with `index out of range [2] with length 2` on any screen whose DiffIntvl is not {0,0}.
2. Two same-version samples with different column counts: verified panic on `prev.Values[j][l]` when the diff interval covers a column the previous (narrower) sample does not have.

Both are pre-existing and live in internal/stat, outside this task's scope; recorded here so the [020] reachability note in the task file is not read as "unreachable".
findings.impact: Runtime panic (process abort) while parsing a crafted archive, for every report type with a non-empty DiffIntvl. Availability only.
findings.recommendation: When [020] is paid down, add to `validate()`: `if r.Ncols != len(r.Cols) { return fmt.Errorf("invalid number of columns") }`, and bound the diff loop by `len(prev.Values[j])` as well as `curr.Ncols`. No change requested in Task 03.

findings.title: Archive-controlled strings are written to the terminal without neutralizing control/escape sequences
findings.description:
printStatSample - the function this task modifies - writes cell values straight to the writer with `fmt.Fprintf(w, "%-*s", ...)` / `%s` (report/report.go:619, 624). Those values come from the archive: query text, application_name, wait events. A recording produced by someone else can therefore embed ESC/CSI/CR sequences that repaint or overwrite already-printed lines, hide rows, or set the terminal title when the report is viewed in a terminal (pgcenter itself already emits ANSI, so the stream is not treated as plain text). The truncation path bounds length, not content, and it slices on byte offsets so a multi-byte rune can also be split into invalid UTF-8.

Pre-existing and identical in top/; not introduced by this diff and not required for Task 03's acceptance criteria. Flagged because printStatSample is the audited function and because the trust model here is explicitly "an archive from a colleague".
findings.impact: A crafted recording can make the rendered report misrepresent its own contents to the operator (rows overwritten or hidden by CR/CSI sequences), which undermines the report as troubleshooting evidence. No code execution in mainstream terminals.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening, separate from this task: strip or escape C0/C1 control characters (everything below 0x20 except none, plus 0x7F, plus ESC-introduced sequences) from archive-sourced values in a single helper shared by report/ and top/ before printing, e.g. `strings.Map(func(r rune) rune { if r < 0x20 || r == 0x7f { return -1 }; return r }, s)`. Doing so would also make truncation rune-aware.
findings.cwe: CWE-150 (Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences)
